title: Drawing near
hook: a sacred hadith: My servant draws near with extra deeds until I love him, and become the hearing he hears with
tomorrow: the mistake you replay at 2 a.m. what if it's already pardoned?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a good intention counts: meant is written, done is multiplied, and a stopped wrong becomes a good. Intending counts. Today, what comes after the intending.

Musicians say the scales are the job, and the extra hour nobody asked for is where it starts to sing. Yesterday's question: the duties or the extras, which brings you closer? Hadith thirty-eight, a sacred hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, answers both, in order. My servant draws near to Me with nothing more beloved to Me than what I made a duty. And My servant keeps drawing near with extra deeds until I love him.
screen: `THE SCALES, THEN THE EXTRA HOUR.` → `THE DUTIES: MOST BELOVED.` → `THE EXTRAS: UNTIL I LOVE HIM.`

segments.voice: The extras are nawafil: voluntary prayers, fasts, charity, remembrance, the things nobody requires. Then the line people argue about: and when I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he holds, his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will give him. Two readings live inside the tradition. One, from commentators like Ibn Rajab: Allah guards and guides that person's senses, so he hears, sees and does what Allah loves, and his prayers are answered. Its best case: it keeps the plain meaning of a servant who stays a servant, and fits the very next line, if he asks Me. The other, from some Sufi teachers: love that close changes who is acting; the servant's own wanting thins out until what moves him is what Allah wants. Its best case: the hadith chose first-person, intimate words on purpose, and they shouldn't be flattened. These teachers too insist the servant never becomes God. And the Qur'an, in Pickthall's words, says Allah is already "nearer to him than his jugular vein." Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: in this hadith, the nearness is already there; the drawing near is ours to do.
screen: `NAWAFIL: THE EXTRAS.` · `I AM HIS HEARING.` · `READING ONE: GUARDED AND GUIDED.` · `READING TWO: HIS WANTING THINS OUT.` · then, large: `DRAWN NEAR.`

segments.voice: If you pray, choose a short phrase Muslims say as a voluntary extra, subhanallah, glory be to Allah, and say it softly on each out-breath for the sit. If not, choose one word you'd like to grow toward, patience or kindness, and say that softly instead. One small extra, said out loud, nobody asking.
Drawing near: first through the duties, most beloved, then through the extras, until love. Hadith thirty-eight, in Allah's own voice.
Keep this one: drawn near, by the duties first and the small extras after. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims build voluntary acts on top of the required ones: extra prayers around the five daily prayers, voluntary fasts, charity beyond zakah, and phrases of remembrance like subhanallah.

options: she thinks people can turn into God.

original.note: Arabic: he draws near to Me with the extras. yataqarrabu, drawing near; nawafil, voluntary deeds.

trapdoor: what you thought: do extra religious stuff and God likes you more.
what it means: duties first, then extras, and the drawing near ends in Allah's love and care.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari 6502, a hadith qudsi; Ibn Rajab's reading of guarded senses, the Sufi reading of a self that thins out, and both keeping servant and Lord distinct.
guess: coming closer to Allah, duties first, then extras
a journey on foot to a holy place far away
the moment of death, when the soul goes to God

chat.says: finals week. i want to add a voluntary fast. dad says nail the five prayers first. who's right?
options: Both, in order: duties are most loved, extras build on them. Start where you're steady.
You. Anyone can do the basics; real closeness is only ever in the extra stuff.
Your dad. Extras are optional, so they don't actually bring anyone closer.
chat.meaning: Nothing is more beloved than the duties, and the extras keep you drawing near until love. Both, in that order.

nawafil.meaning: voluntary deeds beyond the required ones

Ibn Rajab.meaning: a scholar who wrote a famous commentary on the forty

Sufi.meaning: belonging to Islam's mystical tradition of the heart

subhanallah.meaning: glory be to Allah; a phrase of remembrance
